transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-20 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~46 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Liam (CTO), Priya (SRE), Ava (Product), Ben (Data Eng)

Auto-generated summary: quick console walkthrough focusing on tracing and request logs, some cross talk and a demo of error-analysis.

[00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, this is Maya on the SE side, we'll take you through the Console tracing and request logs features and show debugging flows.
[00:12] Liam Chen: Hey thanks, yes we're particularly interested in connecting logs from our gateway and being able to trace down which prompt caused an error or hallucination.
[00:20] Maya Lin: Yeah totally, that's the core of this walkthrough. We'll show how our tracing links from a high-level request down to token-level latencies, and how request logs let you replay and debug.
[00:35] Priya Narang: Quick context, we run a mix of hosted and some in-house inference for PHI workloads, so data residency and KMS are big for us. We'll ask about private deployment later.
[00:48] Jordan Park: Noted. We'll highlight private options and how audit logs/KMS integrate.
[00:55] Ava Martinez: Timeline-wise we're evaluating now, pilot in a couple weeks if things look good.

[01:10] Maya Lin: Ok jumping into the Console — this is the tracing view. Top left you see a heatmap of request latency and error rates by route. (screen share noise) Apologies for small text, tell me if I need to zoom.
[01:30] Ben Ortiz: Can you show how this ties back to the payload? For us the prompt sometimes comes from a multi-turn session stored in our DB.
[01:38] Maya Lin: Yep, there's an expand icon on each trace that surfaces the request metadata: route, model version, input size, KV cache hit rate (approx), and then the raw input — although note we mask PII depending on customer config.
[01:54] Jordan Park: Also call out that tracing supports custom attributes you can add at the SDK level — like session id or user id — which makes searching easier.
[02:05] Liam Chen: How often are traces sampled? We don't want to overload telemetry costs.
[02:12] Maya Lin: By default sampling's adaptive — higher sampling on errors and tail-latency. You can set static rates per route; for pilot we usually suggest 5-10% and full capture for errors.

[02:35] Priya Narang: Error analysis — show us how you group errors. We saw spikes but haven't been able to attribute to model rollouts.
[02:43] Maya Lin: Sure. Here's the error-analysis tab — it buckets by exception type, model response code, and then we do prompt-diff clustering to show similar failing prompts. It's heuristic and slightly fragile, e.g., proper nouns sometimes get fuzzy.
[03:05] Jordan Park: One common pattern we see is format errors after a prompt change; the console surfaces examples and you can open the raw request to replay.
[03:18] Ava Martinez: Replay — does that hit your hosted endpoints or can we replay into our dedicated pool?
[03:25] Maya Lin: Good question. Replay can target whichever environment you have integrated: hosted, dedicated, or private. For dedicated we route to their reserved capacity and respect their rollout config.

[03:45] Liam Chen: About request logs ingestion: what formats, how do we ship? We use Fluentd into S3 today.
[03:52] Maya Lin: Two options: direct ingestion via SDK/webhook or S3/Cloud Storage pickup. We support gzipped newline-delimited JSON with a small mapping script; we also provide a sample Fluentd config in the docs.
[04:10] Ben Ortiz: Great, we'll want to keep logs on-prem for a bit — data residency.
[04:15] Jordan Park: We can configure region-specific storage and optional customer-managed KMS; that's part of the Private offering.

[04:30] Maya Lin: Now I'm going to drill into an individual trace — you'll see timing bars for token-gen, KV cache hits, and kernel time. Note sometimes the kernel-time label will say 'native' or 'optimized' depending on the model/quantization.
[04:50] Priya Narang: We noticed earlier a lot of tail latency during long contexts. Can you show cache metrics?
[04:57] Maya Lin: Sure — KV cache hit rate shows as a percent per route; in this example the cache warmed up after 3 requests and tail latency dropped by ~45%. We also surface cold-start indicators from spilled KV to CPU.

[05:20] Liam Chen: Any gotchas with quantized models and tracing? We've seen weird tokens and tokenization mismatches.
[05:27] Maya Lin: Tokenization mismatches are more on the model/serving layer; tracing will show the raw tokenized sequence we saw, which helps debug misaligned decoding. For quantized models we annotate the trace with the runtime path used (e.g., 4-bit kernel).

[05:50] Jordan Park: Shifting to error grouping — here's a cluster labeled 'wrong-entity-extraction', you can click and get top 10 examples, affected model versions, and a diff view that highlights prompt changes.
[06:08] Ava Martinez: That diff view looks useful. Can we export examples to a CSV for internal triage?
[06:14] Maya Lin: Yep export is available; you can also hook an integration to your issue tracker to create tickets per cluster.

[06:30] Priya Narang: Walk me through a debugging flow — we want to start from an alert, get to root cause, and implement a fix with minimal blast radius.
[06:40] Maya Lin: Example flow: alert fires on a high error rate -> open cluster in Console -> filter by route and model version -> pick representative example -> open raw request + environment metadata -> run a replay in sandbox mode against a canary model or different quantization. If replay fails, you can open a rollback to previous version from the rollouts UI.
[07:05] Liam Chen: Rollback from console, nice. Does rollback trigger our infra hooks? We need to run pre-deploy checks.
[07:12] Jordan Park: Rollouts integrate with your CI/CD via webhooks; you can enforce pre-deploy gates. For Dedicated/Private we also support manual approval flows.

[07:30] Ben Ortiz: On replay, do we get identical inputs — including headers and session context?
[07:36] Maya Lin: We capture request metadata but for sensitive headers we mask by default; you can opt-in for full capture under strict controls. Replay includes input, route, model version, and environment flags.

[07:55] Ava Martinez: Could you show a request-log search? We want to search by user_id and session id.
[08:02] Maya Lin: Sure — in request logs you can query with custom attributes; here's a search for session_id=abc123 that returns a paginated list of requests with latency and error flags.
[08:18] Priya Narang: Pagination and retention — what's default retention for request logs in hosted?
[08:24] Jordan Park: Default retention is 30 days on hosted; we offer longer retention as an add-on or via S3 export. Dedicated/Private can manage retention per customer policy.

[08:40] Liam Chen: Security: audit logs and SSO. We need to show auditors how access is granted.
[08:47] Jordan Park: Console integrates with SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. Audit logs record user actions (view/export/replay) and are available for export. We'll include the compliance pack in the follow-up.

[09:05] Maya Lin: Now a quick demo of an error replay: selecting a failing trace... hitting replay in sandbox mode... you can see the generated output in the console, with token timings. Note the sandbox uses isolated resources so it won't affect production quotas.
[09:30] Ben Ortiz: In sandbox can we change the model variant — like swap to a faster quantized variant?
[09:36] Maya Lin: Yes you can pick a variant; the console will show the predicted latency delta and cost delta. That's part of the Optimize recommendations we hinted at earlier.

[09:55] Ava Martinez: There was mention of automatic fallback policies earlier — show that.
[10:02] Maya Lin: Fallbacks are route-level policies: if the primary model exceeds latency SLO or errors above threshold, we can route to a cheaper/faster variant or to a cached response. The routing rules are programmable and support canary percentages.

[10:20] Liam Chen: From an observability standpoint, can we hook Prometheus metrics or alerts?
[10:26] Jordan Park: Yes we export metrics to Prometheus and support alerting via PagerDuty/Webhook. Tracing spans can also be exported to your APM if needed.

[10:40] Priya Narang: For pilot we'll need a small benchmark: 1k QPS burst, mixed prompt lengths. Can you run a bench or do we run with a template?
[10:49] Maya Lin: We have a benchmark template; Maya to share the spreadsheet. For Dedicated pilots we can run a joint benchmark using your sample logs to size the pool.

[11:05] Liam Chen: Cost — how do we reason about request-logs storage and tracing overhead?
[11:10] Jordan Park: Tracing is metered separately and you can set sampling; request logs storage is either in-console billed or exported to your bucket; we'll provide cost estimates in the proposal.

[11:25] Ava Martinez: Any limitations with private deployments around tracing?
[11:30] Maya Lin: For Private we provide the same Console surface but telemetry can be kept on-prem. There are some connector differences for S3 vs internal object stores, but we work through that in onboarding.

[11:50] Priya Narang: One more onre: can you correlate user complaints from Zendesk to raw traces?
[11:56] Maya Lin: Yes — you can add external ticket id as an attribute and search by it; we also have a small integration for Zendesk to auto-link tickets to traces.

[12:10] Jordan Park: Wrapping up — quick recap. We covered tracing UI, error clustering, request logs ingestion paths, replay/debugging, and rollouts/fallbacks.
[12:22] Liam Chen: Good, next for us is to share sample logs and finalize pilot scope.
[12:28] Ava Martinez: We'll confirm internal stakeholders and timeline.

[12:36] Jordan Park: Next steps: I'll send SOC2/ISO, Maya will share bench template and Fluentd sample, and we'll schedule pilot kickoff week of 3/30.
[12:48] Priya Narang: Thanks all, this was helpful.
[12:52] Maya Lin: Thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[12:58] Jordan Park: Bye everyone.
